content.user_title: Execute Plans with Subagent Review Gates
content.value_statement: Large plans can drift when one agent carries too much context. This skill runs each independent task through a fresh subagent and review step.
actual_capabilities: Guides execution of an existing implementation plan task by task.
Uses a fresh subagent for each independent task to reduce context pollution.
Adds code review after every task before continuing.
Defines how to handle critical, important, and minor review feedback.
Requires a final review before branch completion.
limitations: It depends on a clear plan created before execution starts.
It is not designed for tightly coupled tasks that require constant shared context.
It increases subagent usage and may cost more than manual execution.
It describes a workflow and does not include executable automation code.

use_cases.title: Implement a planned feature safely
use_cases.description: A developer can execute independent feature tasks while keeping review checkpoints between changes.

use_cases.title: Maintain quality during rapid iteration
use_cases.description: A technical lead can ask for subagent work and review after each task before the next task begins.

use_cases.title: Reduce context overload on large plans
use_cases.description: A solo builder can isolate each task in a fresh subagent and keep the main session focused on coordination.

prompt_templates.title: Start from a plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven development to execute this plan. Create tasks, run one task at a time, and review each result before continuing.

prompt_templates.title: Run with test focus
prompt_templates.scenario: Execute a plan where tests are important.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven development for this plan. Ask each subagent to write or update tests, verify results, and report changed files.

prompt_templates.title: Handle review feedback
prompt_templates.scenario: Continue after a reviewer finds issues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Continue the subagent-driven development workflow. Fix critical and important review issues before starting the next task.

prompt_templates.title: Complete the full workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Finish a multi-task implementation with final review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use subagent-driven development through all remaining tasks. Run review after each task, then run a final review before finishing the branch.

output_examples.input: Execute my plan with subagent-driven development.
output_examples.output: The assistant creates a task list, dispatches Task 1 to a fresh subagent, reviews the result, fixes issues, then continues.

output_examples.input: The reviewer found an important issue after Task 2.
output_examples.output: The assistant pauses the sequence, dispatches a focused fix subagent, verifies the fix, then marks Task 2 complete.
The assistant dispatches a final reviewer, checks plan coverage, and moves into the branch finishing workflow.

best_practices: Use this skill only after a concrete implementation plan exists.
Run tasks sequentially unless the plan clearly prevents conflicts.
Fix critical and important review findings before continuing.
anti_patterns: Do not use this workflow when the plan still needs design decisions.
Do not skip review between tasks to save time.
Do not dispatch multiple implementation subagents when they may edit the same files.

faq.question: What problem does this skill solve?
faq.answer: It helps execute implementation plans while keeping each task isolated and reviewed before the next task starts.

faq.question: Does this skill write code by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides a workflow for using subagents, tests, reviews, and final validation.

faq.question: When should I avoid this skill?
faq.answer: Avoid it when tasks are tightly coupled, the plan is unclear, or you need design discussion first.

faq.question: Why use a fresh subagent for each task?
faq.answer: Fresh subagents reduce context pollution and help each task follow only its own requirements.

faq.question: How does the review step work?
faq.answer: After each task, a reviewer checks the implementation against the plan and reports issues by severity.

faq.question: Is this useful for Claude Code and Codex users?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow is written for agentic coding tools that can delegate tasks and review code changes.
